Make your resume look good. Don’t use any silly fonts but choose one that’s a little different and professional. I use Garamond. Make sure your layout is clear and direct. Try to include only jobs pertinent to the one you’re applying for. If they ask about any gaps in your resume be prepared to answer with something intelligent: you were focusing on school, looking for a career change, etc.

Use cover letters. Type up a basic template and switch out the names accordingly.

Don’t be afraid to embellish a little. Don’t flat out lie, but use language in the interview that demonstrates you held some level of responsibility and you were depended on. Don’t get flamboyant with your resume. The example is the Darryl scene from the office— don’t try and trick the interviewer with coded language. If you were a janitor, write “janitor”. Don’t write “custodial specialist”.

During the interview, be cool, and personable. Don’t be stiff. Don’t make an ass of yourself, but if you want a glass of water when they offer, accept it.

Don’t smoke any cigarettes before the interview. Smell nice.

With respect to attire, I believe it’s much more important to look good than it is to wear the “standard” khakis and a button down, especially if what you have is ill-fitting. If you have to choose between ill-fitting dress pants that don’t match with your shirt, then wear some nice jeans. Get a professional shirt, get a haircut, and look good. Think Aspen-casual. Now if you’re going for an executive position, then get yourself a suit that fits.

Shave your face.

Bring copies of your resume.

Be prepared for the following questions: “what are your greatest strengths?” “What are your greatest weaknesses?” And “why should we hire you?” Don’t be afraid to brag. Tell them directly what you’re good at and what methods work for you. If you can do this you’ll notice that at some point during the interview it’ll switch from 20 questions to a conversation. That’s where you want to be.

You’re there to make them money based on your skills. Don’t be afraid to ask for the salary you want. If they can’t meet it, then ask what positions in the company could meet that salary.

Don’t fidget. Bring a pen and paper to write stuff down.

Learn something about the company and ask questions about it. Do your research!

Good luck, bro.
